PullRequest.Title: Respect file and input read-only state in the Markdown editor
PullRequest.Body:
﻿## Problem

The Markdown editor (`vscode.markdown.editor`) did not know when its backing file or editor input was read-only (for example, a file matching `files.readonlyInclude`, a read-only file system / permissions, a session read-only override, or a Git staged `git:` revision). Users could switch the mode toggle to Editing and type into read-only or staged documents without any warning — either showing stale edits that were not actually staged or losing edits silently on close.

Fixes #332117
Fixes #348934

## Changes

- **Custom editor read-only proposed API (`customEditorReadonly`):**
  - Added `WebviewPanel.isReadonly` and `WebviewPanel.onDidChangeReadonly` in `src/vscode-dts/vscode.proposed.customEditorReadonly.d.ts` and registered the proposal in `extensionsApiProposals.ts`.
  - Forwarded the custom editor model/input read-only state (and live changes from `ICustomEditorModel.onDidChangeReadonly` and `onMove`) from `MainThreadCustomEditors` → `ExtHostCustomEditors` → `ExtHostWebviewPanel`.
- **Markdown editor integration (`extensions/markdown-language-features`):**
  - Propagated `documentReadonly` through initial webview state and `configurationChanged` notifications so live changes (such as **File: Toggle Active Editor Read-only in Session** or `files.readonlyInclude` edits) update open editors immediately.
  - Forced read mode and hid the read/edit mode toggle (`showReadonlyToggle: false`) while `documentReadonly` is true, without overwriting the user's global `markdown.editor.readonly` preference.
  - Guarded `TextDocumentSync.applyEdits`, workspace edits (rename, completions, image paste), history (undo/redo), task checkbox toggles, and embedded code block edits against mutating read-only documents.
  - Displayed a localized `"Cannot edit in read-only editor"` toast when the user attempts to edit a read-only document (typing, deleting, pasting/cutting, clicking task checkboxes, or triggering edit commands).

## Screenshots (Code OSS)

## Validation

- `dw run .tmp/dev-workspace.ts typecheck` (all 6 Markdown tsconfigs) — passed
- `dw run .tmp/dev-workspace.ts coreTypecheck` — passed
- `node build/oxlint.ts` on all 13 changed TypeScript files — 0 issues
- `scripts/test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadCustomEditors.test.js` — 16/16 passed (includes new read-only propagation test)
- `dw run .tmp/dev-workspace.ts markdownScriptTests` — 18/18 passed
- `dw run .tmp/dev-workspace.ts markdownExtensionTests` — 220/220 passed (includes new read-only bridge test)
- Verified live in Code OSS: `files.readonlyInclude`, dynamic **File: Toggle Active Editor Read-only in Session**, and Git staged revision (`staged.md (Index)`).

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a Markdown/custom editor, including Git staged revisions and inline or side-by-side diffs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing model resolution and custom-editor resolution must complete; Markdown initially renders the existing serialized document and then connects its content session. The new readonly calculation reads the already-resolved model synchronously. Contributed static code-block provider loading is started without awaiting it on the editor-open path; affected blocks can wait for their provider separately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the text model through the file/content provider, potentially loading document bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model creation per uncached resource/viewType entry, with underlying text models acquired by canonical URI and concurrent acquisitions sharing references. Warm existing models are retained rather than recreated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical model acquisition and resource grouping. The new readonly read does not resolve metadata or read file contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited prerequisite to custom-editor resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: For a cold staged git: document, obtain content with git show --textconv; index metadata can use git ls-files --stage followed by git cat-file -s.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One content command per issued provider read; index stat uses two sequential commands per issued stat. Actual cold read/stat count depends on existing file-service resolution. Warm canonical model reuse avoids a new model load. No commands are issued by isReadonly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The staged document was loaded through the same Git provider and commands.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing cold staged-document loading prerequisite; subprocess count is unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the custom editor in the extension host, passing its initialization data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution call per ordinary or inline panel, or one paired call after both side-by-side handles are available. A boolean is added to the existing initialization data.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same resolution calls, grouping, and awaiting, without the readonly boolean.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited extension-host resolution; no additional round trip for initial readonly state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-stringify and URI-encode initial document/configuration data into webview HTML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing full-document serialization per panel initialization or HTML reload. Added boolean and localized message have constant size independent of document length.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same document content and configuration were serialized into HTML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous HTML construction on initialization; no new full-document copy or increased serialization frequency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read static provider HTML and, when needed, dynamically resolved provider resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential read per static contribution per existing load invocation; dynamic successful resolutions and in-flight work are cached by provider/document/language, while absent or failed descriptors are evicted. The diff changes none of these keys or calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same loading, cache invalidation, resource reads, and provider scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Static loading is not awaited before initial HTML construction; individual code blocks may depend on descriptor availability.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct canonical document URIs, resource/viewType model keys, open webview panels, document bytes, static provider contributions, and distinct provider/document/language keys. An inline diff retains up to two distinct resources; side-by-side panels share model entries and issue one paired resolution.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model acquisitions can overlap across distinct resources and share pending models for identical keys. Additional diff resources are awaited in the existing sequence; side-by-side resolution waits for both handles and starts once. Static provider files load sequentially per invocation. Git read-only operations are asynchronous and are not newly limited or expanded by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Custom models retain promise entries keyed by resource/viewType; failed entries are removed. Canonical URI text-model acquisition shares underlying models. Readonly uses existing provider lookup, session overrides, cached glob matchers, and last-resolved file stat rather than fresh I/O. Provider descriptor caches and negative-result behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff and surrounding resolver/provider code establish unchanged expensive-boundary counts; the added initial state is constant-sized and uses an existing model.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings were measured. External Markdown editor implementation and telemetry SDK internals are outside the inspected source; no changed heavyweight initialization mechanism was established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: existing cold-load costs remain, while readonly metadata is piggybacked on existing initialization calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Toggle session read-only, change files.readonly settings, or change filesystem-provider capabilities with multiple open editors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing readonly change reaches synchronous main-thread listeners, which compute and compare state. Changed panels receive extension-host notification; ready Markdown panels receive configuration notification before their local mode updates. No document reload, provider refresh, or content read is added to this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve file metadata when the existing session-toggle command requests readonly='toggle'.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing metadata resolution for the toggled resource; no metadata call is added for each panel or readonly listener.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same toggle command resolved metadata before changing the session override.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited toggle prerequisite, before notifications are emitted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver a changed readonly boolean to the corresponding extension-host panel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new small notification per panel whose state changes; unchanged states and unrelated provider schemes do not emit it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No custom-editor readonly notification was sent to extensions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required propagation to extensions, without an added awaited round trip in the emitter callback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send existing bounded editor configuration, now including documentReadonly, to a ready Markdown webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded configuration notification per changed ready Markdown panel; before readiness the latest state is sent through the existing ready handler. Not one call per block, task, or document character.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Configuration notifications were sent on readiness and relevant configuration/EOL changes, but not on backing readonly transitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local mode changes consume this notification; no full HTML reconstruction or content sync is triggered by readonly itself.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enqueue an existing mode-change telemetry event through the extension telemetry SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one constant-sized event per actual effective mode transition in a non-diff session. Same-mode calls return without sending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Mode telemetry was emitted for user mode changes, not backing readonly transitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No network completion is awaited before configuration propagation; delivery/aggregation belongs to the existing SDK.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of resolved panels affected by a model change or provider scheme, and the subset whose effective readonly state actually changes. Configuration changes can affect many models; identical-state notifications are suppressed per panel.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Emitter callbacks run synchronously in sequence; changed-state IPC notifications are asynchronous and not globally throttled. Work is proportional to affected panels, with per-panel equality suppression. No new collection of heavyweight operations is launched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Main thread, extension-host panel, Markdown provider, and webview compare the latest boolean against stored state. Readonly checks reuse existing cached provider/configuration/last-stat state. They do not invalidate code-block caches or reread content.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the three explicit equality checks and ready gating bound the notification cardinality; configuration payload and telemetry event have constant size.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large open-panel counts and transition frequency are unmeasured. The extra bounded notifications implement the new feature; no expensive redundant operation was identified.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: intentional state propagation adds bounded per-changed-panel messages, not document/block-scaled fan-out, eager reads, or full reconstruction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type, cut/paste text, toggle tasks, edit embedded code, or invoke undo/redo in a read-only or writable editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Read-only input takes local guards and feedback instead of mutating the document. Writable input retains the existing content synchronization and undo/redo path. New checks return cached booleans and perform no service read.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update a reusable toast and two fixed live-region nodes, and replace its hide timer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three live-region/container nodes per editor, at most one lazy toast, and one active timer. Each attempted readonly edit performs bounded DOM writes plus a nearest-editable-ancestor query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No readonly toast/live-region feedback or these capture handlers existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous input feedback; no geometry read, forced-layout read/write sequence, or full-document traversal is introduced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply synchronized writable text edits through the existing backing-document adapter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing edit-batch calls for writable documents; the new panel.isReadonly getter is local and readonly batches return false before applying edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All incoming batches reached the backing-document applyEdits adapter without the new guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing edit commit prerequisite; readonly guards do not add an awaited read or boundary call.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Route undo/redo to the workbench command and authoritative undo service after draining pending writes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing command invocation per accepted writable history request; readonly requests now skip draining/command execution, and workbench readonly inputs skip undo/redo.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same drain and command path without readonly guards.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing serialization behind pending writes for writable history. No additional wait is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Input event frequency and DOM ancestor depth; document/task/code-block count does not multiply feedback allocations. Writable edit payload scales with the existing edit batch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Feedback executes on the webview input thread; timeout replacement bounds pending feedback work to one timer. Existing document/history sequencing is preserved. The readonly autorun can correct a false mode once, not run an unbounded toggle cycle.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Feedback nodes are reused and timers are replaced, not accumulated. The model/panel boolean is already synchronized. Writable editing and history retain their existing synchronization state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: local DOM writes are constant-cardinality, no layout measurements were added, and both writable mutation and history call paths are unchanged except guards.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Input/browser timing is unmeasured. Ancestor queries and small feedback updates alone do not establish user-visible jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: readonly edits suppress expensive mutation work; feedback is small, reused, and cleaned up.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rename, request/accept completions, or paste multiple media files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing handlers drain content synchronization and check session/current-document state before provider commands or clipboard/file work. Readonly predicates now reject requests before those expensive steps and reject a later workspace apply if state changed in flight.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One prepare command and one rename-provider command per accepted rename flow; one completion-provider call for the list and a second on acceptance. Existing provider fan-out behind these commands is unchanged; readonly requests are rejected before issuance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical provider command cardinality and ordering, without documentReadonly in the active predicate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited provider work before applying the operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and apply one grouped WorkspaceEdit for rename, completion, or media paste.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing applyEdit per accepted operation, containing all affected edits/files; not a new call per entry. Readonly state skips it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same grouped applyEdit and edit telemetry, without the new readonly guard.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited commit step for writable operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer clipboard media in bounded base64 chunks from the webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sum of ceil(file.size / 256 KiB) calls for writable media materialization. Chunks are sequential per file, and existing materialization loops files sequentially. Readonly requests do not reach transfer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical chunk size, calls, allocations, and sequencing for accepted media paste.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited media materialization before the grouped WorkspaceEdit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat candidate destination filenames and create media files through the grouped workspace edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing stat attempts per candidate until an unused destination is found, unless overwrite avoids stat; per-paste usedPaths prevents reuse. File creation occurs for each copied media entry in one WorkspaceEdit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same candidate search and grouped file creation for editable paste.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited destination selection/materialization/commit. Readonly predicates stop new requests before these operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Rename's affected workspace resources and edits; completion list size and acceptance resolve prefix; pasted media count, total bytes, 256 KiB chunks, and existing destination-name collisions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider requests use existing per-session stale/current checks; media cancels the prior pending paste. Destination discovery uses existing Promise.all across files, then file materialization and chunks are sequential. No newly increased concurrency or calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Rename/completion session objects and media cancellation ownership are unchanged. Existing media destination deduplication is per paste. No cache is bypassed or introduced, and no retry loop is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced guards precede the unchanged service and media operations; grouped edit and chunk cardinalities are explicit in code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency, list/workspace size, media bytes, and collision prevalence are unmeasured; all scaling work predates the diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff narrows reachability of existing expensive workflows and does not amplify their fan-out, serialization, or concurrency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close, dispose, reload, or Save As a custom/Markdown editor and transfer ownership
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Disposal removes new listeners, feedback nodes, and timer along with existing session cleanup. Existing Markdown HTML reloads reset transports and refresh providers; readonly transitions themselves do not reload HTML. Save As continues to return a target resource for normal editor resolution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing provider resource rereads on HTML reload, and existing Save As/file-model resolution operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Provider reads remain one per static contribution per existing reload invocation. Save As retains its existing save and target-resource acquisition path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same reload triggers, provider refresh, Save As, and target-resource model resolution existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unchanged reload/provider and save prerequisites; added readonly state does not schedule extra reloads.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose the existing panel/webview and code-block host transports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing panel disposal and per-live-transport cleanup calls. The new readonly emitter/listeners and feedback cleanup add no disposal RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same panel and host-transport disposal operations, without the new local readonly resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing teardown path; new cleanup is synchronous and constant per panel.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live panels and their lifetime; repeated open/close and existing HTML reload frequency. New retained state is constant per live panel, not proportional to edit history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: New cleanup is synchronous. Ordinary watcher replacement removes the old subscription. Inspected the async onMove callback as a possible disposal race, but Markdown does not supply moveCustomTextEditor, and CustomEditorInput's stored _moveHandler has no invocation in the inspected repository, so no reachable new retention scenario was established there.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: New model readonly and provider-capability subscriptions are removed on input/webview disposal and resolve failure. The extension-host emitter is registered for disposal; Markdown removes its panel subscription and local DOM/timer state. Existing model reference and provider cache ownership remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for normal lifetime cleanup and unchanged reload behavior. Insufficient live call-path evidence for an asynchronous move-listener leak, so it was not reported.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repeated session and reload timing is unmeasured. External future consumers of the proposed API or dormant move hook cannot establish a present regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: new retained resources are bounded to the live panel and have explicit teardown; potential dormant-hook behavior lacks a realistic reachable trigger.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 19 changed files and every diff page against base 0cd87f75609c475a29750f73668e0db2d84418c3. Traced initial resolution, staged Git reads, readonly transitions, input feedback, document/history edits, rename/completion/media operations, and lifetime/reload ownership. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression qualified, and no concrete performance regression fix with sufficient provenance/symptom evidence was identified. Static review only; external Markdown editor and telemetry SDK implementation costs were not measured.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
